StaceviÄius / LRT Lithuanian and Polish border officials are meeting Thursday to discuss ways to make inspections at their shared border more efficient while Poland maintains temporary controls aimed at curbing secondary migration, Lithuaniaâs interior minister said. Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas said the two countries should seek to streamline inspections by focusing on higher-risk vehicles and cargo while allowing regular travellers to cross more quickly. âTrucks and cargo vans can be inspected, but when we see two people traveling for business, holidays or other purposes, or perhaps a single person, the check could probably be faster,â Katelynas told reporters. The minister said he raised the issue with Polish counterparts during an informal meeting of European Union justice and home affairs ministers in Dublin last week. According to Katelynas, border officials from both countries were due to meet Thursday to discuss practical measures to reduce queues at the crossing. Poland reintroduced temporary border controls with Lithuania and Germany in July 2025, saying the measures were needed to stem secondary irregular migration. Warsaw argues that migrants who enter Latvia from Belarus travel through Lithuania before attempting to reach Poland and continue onward to Western Europe. The number of migrants intercepted after entering Lithuania from Latvia has risen sharply. In the first half of this year, Lithuanian authorities stopped more than 1,200 people arriving from Latvia, compared with just over 300 during the same period last year. Lithuania has responded by sending teams of border guards to assist Latvian authorities, although it has said it will not provide the full contingent of 100 officers requested by Riga. Katelynas has also not ruled out the possibility that Lithuania could temporarily restore controls on its border with Latvia if secondary migration continues to increase. Under European Union rules, countries in the Schengen area may temporarily reintroduce internal border controls only in exceptional circumstances when public policy or internal security is under threat. https://www.kctv5.com/2026/08/08/lees-su.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - A Lee’s Summit man is facing felony charges after authorities discovered hidden camera footage of a child at a Warsaw lake property, according to the Benton County Sheriff’s Office. Clifton Wade Tucker, 51, is charged with possession of child pornography and invasion of privacy. According to a probable cause statement, guests visiting Tucker’s lake property on July 31 discovered his cellphone in the bathroom displaying a live video feed of a minor undressing. When confronted about the camera feed later that evening, Tucker reportedly fell to his knees crying, begging the victim’s father not to report the incident. He claimed the camera was set up to catch thieves and handed over an SD card. When a detective reviewed the SD card, it revealed footage from a second hidden camera inside the camper’s bedroom, showing a child undressing. Court documents state Tucker is a former law enforcement officer with 10 years of experience who is currently working as an armed guard with access to high-powered firearms. Tucker is being held on a $50,000 bond and is scheduled to appear in court at 9 a.m. on Monday. Copyright 2026 KCTV. All rights reserved. Beállítom A magyar női kosárlabda-válogatott súlyos vereséggel kezdte meg szereplését a berlini világbajnokságon, pénteken 99-53-ra kaptak ki az előzetesen is jóval esélyesebbnek tartott, olimpiai ezüstérmes franciáktól. A magyar csapatnak így nem sikerült jól a 28 éve várt, önmagában is történelmi visszatérés a vb-re, de bőven lesz még esélyük javítani. Szombaton Nigéria, vasárnap Dél-Korea ellen játszik majd a válogatott, és ha legalább a harmadik helyet sikerül megcsípni a csoportban, akkor már játszhatnak a nyolc közé kerülésért. A magyar válogatott nem kezdte rosszul a meccset, a csapat egyértelműen legnagyobb sztárja, a WNBA-ben játszó Juhász Dorka szerezte az első pontot, aztán Takács-Kiss Virág szórt be egy triplát. Innentől viszont a franciák átvették az irányítást, és a negyed végére már 29-11-es vezetéssel mentek. A második negyedben ennél is nyomasztóbb volt a fölényük, és a nagyszünetre gyakorlatilag el is döntötték a meccset, ekkor már 41 pont volt közte. A harmadik negyedben vissza is vettek a tempóból a franciák, de a magyar válogatott így sem tudott feljebb zárkózni, egy ponton már az volt a kérdés, hogy lesz-e 50 is közte. A negyedik negyedben a védekezést már szinte teljesen elengedte a francia csapat, de a pontkülönbségen így sem sikerült kozmetikázni, csak a játékosok statisztikáit segítette, hogy itt 22 pontot dobtak a magyarok. Juhász így dupla dupláig jutott, de ezen kívül sok pozitívumot nem lehetett mondani a meccs után. Völgyi Péter szövetségi kapitány a meccs után azt mondta, kicsit el van keseredve, mert szerinte nem voltak elég agresszívak a játékosai, és az első félidőben túl nagy előnyt adtak a franciáknak, de azt pozitívumként értékelte, hogy a második félidőben tudtak gyakorolni, és készülni a következő meccsükre a kicsit már kiengedő franciák ellen is. Studer Ágnes, a válogatott irányítója azt mondta, fel voltak készülve arra, hogy akár nagyobb zakóba is belefuthatnak ezen a meccsen, de szerinte nem is baj, hogy a franciákkal kezdtek, mert így megtapasztalták, milyen egy olyan csapattal játszani, akik szinte biztosan a top 4-ben lesznek. Juhász a meccs után azt mondta, szerinte kicsit kritikusnak kell lenniük, nem a végeredmény miatt, hanem azért, ahogy kikaptak, ő sem érezte azt, hogy olyan agresszívak lettek volna, amennyire kellett volna. A magyarok sztárja azt mondta, szombaton sem lesz egyszerűbb dolguk Nigéria ellen, de annak más mentalitással kell majd nekimenniük. Nigéria egyébként jóval szorosabb meccsen, 99-81-re kapott ki Dél-Koreától, így kifejezetten fontos lehet majd a holnapi meccs a válogatottnak, mert ha sikerül nyerni, azzal szinte biztosan meglesz a harmadik hely a csoportban, ami már továbbjutást ér. It provides both analytical depth and practical guidance on how culture can function as a strategic, inclusive, and credible instrument of European engagement. Bringing together scholars and practitioners from across Europe, the book examines cultural diplomacy at the intersection of politics, history, media, and the arts. Drawing on empirically rich case studies—from Franco-Romanian exchanges and Polish diasporic networks to TikTok narratives, AI-driven curation, and cultural responses to Russia’s war on Ukraine—the chapters demonstrate how historical awareness, digital literacy, and inclusive narratives can strengthen both internal cohesion and external credibility. It concludes with concrete recommendations for a historically informed, digitally resilient, and values-based European approach. The book is intended for scholars and graduate students in the fields of European studies, international relations, cultural and public diplomacy, media and gender studies, and for policymakers and practitioners serving at cultural institutes, ministries, NGOs, urban networks, and EU bodies. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr93.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, A file photo of Joshimath town, near the site where the helicopter went missing By Zoya Mateen & Nikita Yadav BBC News, Delhi Published 1 hour ago A search for survivors is under way after a helicopter carrying six people, including five pilgrims, crashed in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, officials say. Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter had crashed near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district. Rescue teams have been dispatched to the mountainous area, but the condition of those on board remains unclear. The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact. The cause of the crash is also not yet known. The incident happened amid reports of heavy rain and poor visibility in the region. Uttarakhand, a Himalayan state which borders China and Nepal, is home to some of Hinduism's holiest shrines and attracts millions of pilgrims every year. Badrinath is one of four sacred sites on the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, alongside Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Many devotees travel through steep Himalayan valleys to reach the temples, which are open for only part of the year because of harsh winter conditions. Image source, LightRocket via Getty Images Image caption, Badrinath is one of four temple towns along the Char Dham Yatra pilgrimage route Helicopter services have become increasingly popular among pilgrims seeking to avoid difficult mountain journeys, but their safety has come under scrutiny following a series of accidents. Friday's incident happened amid heavy rain in the region. India's weather department had issued an orange alert for the area, warning of thunderstorms, hail and strong winds. Dhami said , external a joint rescue operation was under way involving the district administration, disaster management department and State Disaster Response Force. "I am continuously monitoring the entire incident," he added. Dhami also said he had ordered that anyone seriously injured be airlifted for treatment. In June 2025 , seven people were killed when a helicopter carrying pilgrims crashed near Kedarnath. Another seven died in a crash on the same pilgrimage route in October 2022. Several other helicopter accidents were reported during the 2025 pilgrimage season, prompting aviation authorities to tighten safety checks and restrict some operations.
